title: How much is your privacy information?

source.relative_path: 2018美赛特等奖/F题4篇/F87280-How much is your privacy information.pdf

context_sources.name: Culnan, consumer attitudes toward secondary information use
Tianqi Chen, introduction to boosted trees
National Bureau of Statistics of China

limitations: The total privacy-cost formula and the risk-amount formula are announced but never printed.
The margin equation is flattened, and the elasticity sign is flipped without derivation.
Only one of the 26 fitted risk functions is shown.
The significance test reports p=0.910 yet claims the hypothesis cannot be accepted, which reverses the stated rule.

tasks: Classify people and fields and price the privacy
Set a pricing rule with demand elasticity
Make the risk factors move with time
Compare age groups and the three neighbouring concepts
Model the network effect of one sale
Price the damage of a leak and the compensation
Advise the government and test stability

section_map.summary: Eight tasks: cost, elasticity, dynamics, network, compensation.
Three citations, 26 indicators in five groups.
Income, risk and relatedness, with AHP and a boosting tree.
Cost plus capped profit, elasticity, three life-cycle stages.
Risk factors become functions of time, one fit shown.
Age scaling, three concepts, small world, prisoner's dilemma.
Long tail against bullwhip, actuarial compensation.
Survey rerun, t-test, four strengths and three weaknesses.
Price, regulation and an emergency plan for the government.
Boosting, small-world, risk and correlation code.

contributions.summary: A third term, relatedness, so equal income and risk need not mean equal cost.
Risk factors turned from constants into fitted functions of time.
A small-world leak read as a prisoner's dilemma that needs a limit.

dependency_graph.handoff: The privacy cost is the base the selling price and the moving risk value build on
The market price is what tempts a member to sell and start a leak
The expected value of the information is the first part of the compensation

assumptions.summary: People in the same conditions guard privacy alike, though reality is roughly normal.
Every member is an economic man and any sale is known at once.
Politics and the military are excluded because the harm cannot be measured.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: China census and consumption, 1997 to 2016, from the national statistics bureau.
Outliers fixed and gaps filled by fuzzy matching, then scaled by z-score.
A 50-person attitude survey, 47 usable, reweights the indicators.

models.summary: Income, risk and Gaussian relatedness over 26 indicators.
Capped margin, elasticity and a decaying risk factor.
Small-world exposure and a four-case dilemma.
Actuarial compensation as value plus further loss.

verification.summary: 500 simulated people price between 600 and 3000 dollars, 5578 if complete.
Repricing on survey weights passes an independent-samples test.

results_trace.summary: Full disclosure prices at 5578 dollars a year.
The total-assets risk factor fits with R-square 0.9779.
Disclosure worsens as both network parameters grow.

writing_logic.summary: The cost is split into three parts before any formula.
Indicators are split by whether they can be measured.
The dilemma is told as a chain that forces the last move.

language_observations.summary: Three citations are lined up to point one way.
A pair of equal people forces the third term.
Two named effects are each tied to a condition.
The emergency plan is four steps in order.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 6-2: relations of the three concepts.
Figure 8-1: a leak cutting the value.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The 600 to 3000 dollar range comes from a simulation, not market data.
The stability verdict contradicts the p-value the paper prints.
The 30 percent margin cap is borrowed from ordinary goods.

weaknesses.summary: Some parameters must be retuned, not everyone accepts the sale, and the fields are incomplete.
Only one of 26 fitted risk functions is shown.
The significance test is reported backwards.

independent_extensions.summary: Print and check the other 25 fitted risk functions.
Fit and report the actuarial parameters.
Recompute the significance test with the correct decision rule.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Limit personal selling to protect the group from one member's sale.
Make the agency pay both the data's value and the further harm.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the printed total-cost formula?
What are the other 25 fitted risk functions?
